facts.raw_span: a 3-month history of rapidly spreading intensively pruritic papules on her extremities
no remarkable medical or family history
not concurrently being treated with any medications
scattered, erythematous, annular papules measuring up to 5 mm wide
a few asymptomatic brown flat papules scattered on her face
the palms, soles, and oral mucosa were not involved
Routine blood, liver and kidney function, antistreptolysin O, C-reactive protein, antinuclear antibody, and rheumatoid factor tests disclosed no abnormal findings
Mild hyperkeratosis accompanied by parakeratosis
Atrophy of the epidermis
Well-developed cornoid lamellae with a decreased granular layer
Individual cell dyskeratosis
Slight infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and eosinophils in the upper dermis

concepts.why: The patient's skin biopsy revealed mild hyperkeratosis, atrophy of the epidermis, well-developed cornoid lamellae, and individual cell dyskeratosis, which are characteristic features of Darier's disease.
The patient's skin biopsy showed mild hyperkeratosis, individual cell dyskeratosis, and a slight infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and eosinophils, which are consistent with Grover's disease.
The patient presented with rapidly spreading intensively pruritic papules on her extremities, which is a characteristic feature of pityriasis rubra pilaris.
The patient's skin biopsy revealed mild hyperkeratosis accompanied by parakeratosis, which is a characteristic feature of parakeratosis variegata.

rationales.F01: Rapidly spreading intensively pruritic papules are more typical of Darier's disease and Grover's disease.
rationales.F05: Asymptomatic brown flat papules on the face are less typical of Darier's disease.
rationales.F08: Mild hyperkeratosis accompanied by parakeratosis is a characteristic feature of Darier's disease and Grover's disease.
rationales.F10: Well-developed cornoid lamellae with a decreased granular layer are a hallmark of Darier's disease.
rationales.F11: Individual cell dyskeratosis is a characteristic feature of Darier's disease.

frontier_selector.rationale: Grover's disease best explains the combination of mild hyperkeratosis, parakeratosis, individual cell dyskeratosis, and slight infiltrate of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and eosinophils in the upper dermis without strong contradictions.
